items.title: Peel Police Service Board Opens September Consultation on Youth Engagement Strategy
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the Peel Police Service Board's governance and human rights committee is hosting a community consultation session on September 15 at Peel Region headquarters to gather public feedback on the police's Youth Engagement Strategy, first launched in March 2025. Mississauga.com reports the session will open with a presentation from police outlining their preliminary youth engagement plan, after which members of the public will each get up to five minutes to make their own presentations to the committee. Police spokesperson Matt Carty told the outlet the service has a long-standing commitment to youth engagement and already runs a range of youth-focused education, prevention and mentorship initiatives, including the Youth in Policing Initiative, G1/G2 Driving, Boys 2 Men, Young Women's Mentorship and partnerships through ProAction Cops and Kids. In an email to Metroland Media cited by Mississauga.com, Carty said the current consultation process is meant to help inform the ongoing evolution of the strategy and support development of a more coordinated youth services model that strengthens how the service engages and supports young people. Mississauga.com notes the strategy has been evolving since its 2025 launch, with police framing the fall consultation as a key step toward shaping that more coordinated approach going forward.

items.title: Canada and Mississauga invest in active transportation infrastructure
items.summary: MISSISSAUGA, ON, Aug. 8 million from the federal government. Fares Al Soud, Member of Parliament for Mississauga Centre and Iqra Khalid, Member of Parliament for Mississauga—Erin Mills; joined Mississauga Councillors Joe Horneck, Ward 6; and Stephen Dasko, Ward 1; to announce joint investments in two active transportation projects. The Culham Trail is a key connector in Mississauga, helping to move more than 500,000 people annually. However, it has suffered severe flood damage, resulting in some portions being closed since 2024. The federal government's investment will help to reconstruct nearly four kilometres of multi-use recreational trail as well as assist in elevating the pathway to prevent future flooding. Additional enhancements will include amenities like new seating and overlook viewing areas, implementation of a bike share system, upgraded signage, and landscaping. North of Lakeshore Road, a new pedestrian and cyclist bridge will be constructed. Spanning approximately 65 metres, the Port Credit Active Transportation Bridge will improve connectivity across the Credit River by linking Port Credit and its GO station to the Mineola West neighbourhood. The bridge deck will provide a comfortable, safe and accessible route for people to walk or ride a bike, while being completely separated from motor vehicle traffic. Active transportation infrastructure like trails and bridges are a convenient and accessible way for residents to get around. By supporting Canadians to walk, run, bike, or roll, we are building strong, vibrant and healthy communities. "Strong communities are healthy communities. Improvements to Culham Trail will make it easier and safer to get around Mississauga.

items.title: Peel Police Data Shows Over 300 Vehicle Thefts Across Mississauga and Brampton in a Single Month
items.summary: According to INsauga, Peel Regional Police data shows more than 300 vehicles were reported stolen across Mississauga and Brampton over the past month. INsauga reports the count covers the 31-day period from July 22 to August 22, during which 304 vehicle thefts were recorded across the two cities. Of those, the outlet reports 175 thefts occurred in Mississauga and 126 in Brampton, with three additional incidents in Caledon falling under Peel police's jurisdiction. INsauga notes this report differs from some previous releases in that Peel Regional Police did not provide an updated breakdown showing how many of the cases had been solved, remained under investigation or were considered unsolved. The absence of that breakdown, according to the outlet, leaves residents without a clear picture of how much progress investigators have made on any of the reported thefts.

items.title: Culham Trail Upgrade and New Port Credit Pedestrian Bridge Get $8.7 Million Federal Boost
items.summary: According to the City of Mississauga, the federal government's Active Transportation Fund is providing $8.7 million to support two major local projects, upgrades to the Culham Trail and construction of a new pedestrian and cycling bridge in Port Credit. The city says the Culham Trail, which stretches through Erindale Park and Riverwood and draws more than 500,000 visitors a year, will see nearly four kilometres of the multi-use recreational trail modernized, along with enhanced flood protection and added amenities such as new seating, an outlook viewing area, a bike share system, upgraded signage and landscaping. According to the city, a new 65-metre bridge designed exclusively for pedestrians and cyclists will span the Credit River between Port Credit Memorial Park and the Port Credit Royal Canadian Legion, north of Lakeshore Road, linking Port Credit and the GO Station with the Mineola West neighbourhood. The city says the bridge was identified as a priority through the Lakeshore Corridor Transportation Improvements study and advances the broader Lakeshore Connecting Communities Master Plan for walking, cycling and access to destinations along the waterfront. Together, the city reports, the two projects are meant to improve connections across Mississauga and make active transportation options easier for residents to choose.

items.title: Mississauga Deferred a 112-Unit Townhouse Proposal After Residents Flagged 19 Requested Variances
items.summary: According to Mississauga.com, the city's committee of adjustment has deferred a request to approve a minor variance that would allow construction of a 112-unit stacked townhouse complex on Bloor Street near Riverspray Crescent. The outlet reports the 0.8-hectare site is zoned for residential highrises and currently holds a 17-storey, 323-unit apartment building that would remain on the property alongside the new townhomes. Mississauga.com reports the committee deferred the landowner's request on August 20 after residents raised objections to the plan. Kim Pines of the Applewood Hills and Heights Residents' Association told the outlet her group welcomed the decision, citing legitimate concerns raised by committee members, including the high number of 19 variances being requested, a lack of communication and consultation with the wider community, and worries about increased parking pressure. According to the Residents' Association, the developer has since agreed to hold a community meeting.

items.title: Christopher Nolan and Denis Villeneuve Have Turned Mississauga's Imax Into Hollywood's Hottest Ticket
items.summary: According to Toronto Star business columnist David Olive, Imax, the Mississauga-based motion picture technology company, is reportedly mulling a sale as its technology becomes the darling of directors such as Christopher Nolan and Denis Villeneuve. Olive writes that this year's most talked-about film, The Odyssey, is the first feature-length movie shot entirely with Imax's 70mm-format cameras, and the immersive experience it delivers alongside the company's most sophisticated projectors and screens is drawing fans hundreds of kilometres to reach one of the 41 Imax screens worldwide fully equipped with its latest technology. The column notes Imax has 1,865 locations across 91 countries, including 43 in Canada, though most of those use traditional digital projection while still carrying the company's trademark floor-to-ceiling, wall-to-wall screens. Major studios including Disney, Paramount and Sony Columbia scramble to book Imax screens for their biggest releases, according to Olive, even though Imax itself does not make movies or operate cinemas. Instead, the Star reports, the company leases its cameras to filmmakers and studios and its screens, projectors and other complex equipment to cinema operators.

items.title: Mississauga's Stonehooker Brewery Set to Shut Down Sept. 7 Without a New Owner
items.summary: According to INsauga, Stonehooker, a craft brewery on Lakeshore Road East in Mississauga, announced Friday that it is winding down operations and could close for good after Labour Day unless a buyer steps forward. INsauga reports the brewery, its physical location and its brewing equipment are all now up for sale, with the company describing itself as retiring from the hospitality business. The outlet notes Stonehooker stressed that its brand is expected to live on regardless, with its beer expected to remain available for the foreseeable future even if the taproom closes. According to INsauga, the brewery's official final day of service is currently scheduled for Monday, September 7, though that date could change if a new owner takes over the business beforehand. INsauga reports the company will not host events after September 7 unless ownership of the business changes hands.

items.title: Battle to be mayor a ‘clear two-way race’ in Mississauga, candidate says
items.summary: The field is set for the mayoral race in Mississauga, with more than a dozen candidates preparing to do battle until voters make the final decision on Oct. 26. m. deadline to register for the 2026 municipal election, 14 names appeared on the list of hopefuls looking to occupy the mayor’s seat in Canada’s seventh-largest city for the next term of council. The two highest-profile candidates — the current mayor, Carolyn Parrish, and her predecessor, Bonnie Crombie — are joined in the contest by city councillors Alvin Tedjo (Ward 2) and Dipika Damerla (Ward 7) and 10 others of varying experience in the realm of political campaigning. ” Crombie, who left the Mississauga mayor’s post in 2024 after 10 years to lead the Ontario Liberals and take a shot at unseating the premier, said she’s looking to reclaim the seat because she believes better days are ahead for the city. “Everywhere I go, I hear the same concerns,” Crombie said in a news release on Friday. “Life has become too expensive. People are worried about safety. Traffic and congestion are taking too much time away from families. And residents want to know that City Hall is focused on getting things done. “I’m running because I believe Mississauga can do better,” she continued.
